# Verifying timed automata against branching real-time hyperproperties is undecidable

HCMTL extends metric temporal logic with quantifiers over executions that branch from previously chosen ones, to express security properties of real-time systems. Deciding whether a timed automaton satisfies an HCMTL sentence is undecidable, already for the fragment HyperMITL, in both the interval-based and point-based semantics.

**Setting (Deka, Zhang, Chadha and Viswanathan).** Formulas of HCMTL (written HCMTL$^*$ in the source) are generated by

$$
\varphi ::= p_\pi \mid \neg p_\pi \mid \varphi \vee \varphi \mid \varphi \wedge \varphi \mid F_I\, \varphi \mid G_I\, \varphi \mid \varphi\, U_I\, \varphi \mid \exists \pi\, \varphi \mid \forall \pi\, \varphi,
$$

where $p$ is an atomic proposition, $\pi$ a path variable and $I$ an interval of nonnegative reals (singular intervals $[t, t]$ allowed); HyperMITL is the fragment in which all quantifiers occur at the front and intervals are non-singular. Systems are timed automata with state labels, clock invariants, guarded edges with resets and final states; executions are finite accepting runs, given as sequences of states with consecutive time intervals. In the interval-based semantics a formula is evaluated at a time $t$ under an assignment of executions to path variables; $\exists \pi\, \varphi$ holds if some accepting execution agreeing with the most recently quantified execution up to time $t$ (any execution at the start) satisfies $\varphi$ at $t$, dually for $\forall \pi$, and the temporal operators constrain times within $t + I$ as in MTL. The *general verification problem* asks, given a timed automaton and an HCMTL sentence, whether the automaton satisfies the sentence at time $0$.

**Theorem (Deka, Zhang, Chadha and Viswanathan).** The general verification problem for HCMTL is undecidable in both the point-based and the interval-based semantics, even for the fragment HyperMITL.

In contrast, the same paper proves that bounded-time verification, which considers only executions and times below a given bound, is decidable in both semantics.

## Expansion

As Ho and coauthors did for HyperMITL model checking, the universality problem for timed automata, which is undecidable, reduces to the general verification problem of HyperMITL in the point-based semantics. The paper shows that the point-based semantics reduces to the interval-based one, so the problem is undecidable there as well; for HCMTL with singular intervals, undecidability in the interval-based semantics also follows from the undecidability of verifying timed automata against MTL.
